component.name: Pipedeck
component.summary: Mix what plays into mixes to hear, record and stream

description.p: A PipeWire mixer for Linux streamers, in the spirit of Elgato Wave Link. Send each application to a channel, then decide how loud every channel is in each mix: what you hear, what goes to the stream and what goes to the call are separate balances.

ul.li: A matrix mixer: channels are rows, mixes are columns, and each cell has its own fader and mute
Effects per channel: noise suppression, equaliser, de-esser and compressor built in, plus VST3 plug-ins and Thimeo's Stereo Tool
Meters on every channel, mix and cell
Stream Deck support through OpenDeck or StreamController, with keys and dials that look like the mixer
Discord calls split into one track per person, with Vesktop
Lives through PipeWire and WirePlumber restarts

screenshot.caption: The mixer: channels in rows, mixes in columns, a fader in each cell that links them

ul.li: A Discord call with Vesktop on no channel puts Vesktop on the voice chat's channel, and says so
Vesktop's plugin is built with a Node.js new enough for it, one that nvm, fnm or volta keeps when the system's is too old
The mixer can be exported to a file and imported from one, in the settings, without the Stereo Tool key
A channel's and a mix's windows scroll when the mixer's window is too short for them
When building Vesktop's plugin fails, Pipedeck says which step failed and why
On OpenDeck, the Call key goes to the call's profile and back
On a Stream Deck +, the call's people are on the dials alone, shown on the touch strip, and the key back to the mixer wears an arrow
A microphone's effects go on the keys left, no longer on a dial
The OpenDeck plugin no longer offers the Call action and Follow calls, which OpenDeck does not let switch profiles
